In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new method of analysis for dioxins and PCBs in food and environmental matrices, and with the application of the results obtained to the assessment of the environmental risk.

the development and implementation of a new method for the analysis of polychlorinated dibenzo-p-dioxins (PCDDs), polychlorinated dibanzo-furans (PCDFs), and coplanar polychlorinated biphenyls (coplanar PCBs) in fish.
the identification of the sources of the contamination and the determination of the fate of the contaminants in the environment.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the concentrations of dioxins in fish and shellfish are low, but not insignificant; the levels of PCBs in fish and shell fish are higher than those of dioxins, and are of more concern to consumers; the levels of dioxins are higher in the flesh of marine fish, compared to shellfish, whereas the reverse is true for PCBs; the levels of both dioxins and PCBs are higher in the edible parts of shellfish than in the flesh of fish
the TEF concept is a valuable approach to estimate the toxic potency of complex mixtures of PCDDs, PCDFs and coplanar PCBs.
there is no clear and consistent evidence that dioxin and furan contamination in the environment is associated with adverse health effects in humans.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
there is a need for more information about the effects of dioxins on wildlife and the environment.
the use of TEFs is not recommended for the assessment of dioxin and furan toxicity in marine species.
the TEF values of PCBs, PCDFs, PCDD/Fs, and PAHs in the Venice lagoons were similar to those in other areas, and the TEFs of PCDD/Fs were higher than those in other areas.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the risk of contamination in the environment is a real one.
the risk to the public is low.
the TEFs are not a reliable way to estimate the risk of PCBs to humans and wildlife, and should be abandoned.
